item.title: Chevy Chase Meltdowns On ‘Community’ Set Included Refusing To Apologize For Throwing The N-Word Around
item.description: While there has been habitual talk about a “Community” movie, there is one original cast member you can likely rule out returning for it, and that would be “SNL” and “National Lampoon’s Vacation” star Chevy Chase. item.title: ‘Stranger Things’ Finale Trailer: The Battle For Hawkins Comes To An Epic Conclusion On New Year’s Eve
item.description: Will Hawkins and our heroic characters survive the finale? You’ll have to tune in to have those answers. The mainline “Stranger Things” series created by The Duffer Brothers and produced by Shawn Levy (“Star Wars: Starfighter”) is coming to an end this week with the finale dropping on Netflix this New Year’s Eve (Wednesday at 5 pm PT) after the rest of the Season 5 episodes dominated streaming records. item.title: ‘Shrinking’ Trailer: Acclaimed Comedy Series Returns January 28 With Guest Stars Jeff Daniels, Michael J. Fox & More Appearing In Season 3
item.description: The GOAT is back! “Shrinking,” starring Jason Segel and Harrison Ford, like “The Morning Show,” has been a hugely popular original show from Apple TV, and the streamer has dropped a look at the third season with a new trailer for the series, created by Bill Lawrence, Brett Goldstein, and Segel, that is set to return next month on the service. item.title: Joseph Kosinski Recalls Brad Pitt & Tom Cruise Almost Starring In His Lost Version Of ‘Ford V Ferrari’
item.description: It’s a bit lost to time (or short-term memory, as everything is on the internet these days), but circa 2013, filmmaker Joseph Kosinski was once set to make a racing movie called “Go Like Hell,” with Brad Pitt and Tom Cruise attached. The project eventually fell apart — getting two megastars in the same film at that moment ballooned the budget beyond what the market could justify. item.title: The Best Posters Of 2025
item.description: For as long as films have existed, the poster has been one of the most effective marketing tools. This is an item that not only teases what to expect from the film, but also can be a work of art in its own right. Nowadays, however, we see quite a few shitty attempts at movie posters. Can it be blamed on laziness, the corporatization of studios, or simply poor artists? Probably a bit of all three. Continue reading The Best Posters Of 2025 at The Playlist.
